questions.stem: Àròkọ tí ó ń sọ ìtàn ohun tí ó ṣẹlẹ̀ lẹ́sẹẹsẹ ni àròkọ
questions.explanation: An essay that recounts events in sequence is narrative (asọ̀tàn).

questions.stem: Lẹ́tà tí akẹ́kọ̀ọ́ kọ sí ọ̀rẹ́ rẹ̀ láti sọ nípa ìsinmi rẹ̀ jẹ́ lẹ́tà
questions.explanation: A letter to a friend is an informal letter (lẹ́tà gbẹ̀fẹ́); letters to offices are formal (àìgbẹ̀fẹ́).

questions.stem: Orí-ọ̀rọ̀ wo ni ó yẹ fún àròkọ aṣàríyànjiyàn?
options: Ọkọ̀ ojú-irin dára ju ọkọ̀ òfuurufú lọ
Bí a ṣe ń se ẹ̀fọ́ rírò
questions.explanation: A claim that one thing is better than another can be argued for or against: argumentative essay.

questions.stem: Mélòó ni kọ́ńsónáǹtì tí ó wà nínú álífábẹ́ẹ̀tì Yorùbá?
questions.explanation: Yoruba has 18 consonant letters (b d f g gb h j k l m n p r s ṣ t w y); 25 is the total number of letters.

questions.stem: Èwo ni kọ́ńsónáǹtì àfèjì-ètè-pè?
questions.explanation: [b] is made with both lips (bilabial); [f] is labiodental, [t] alveolar and [k] velar.

questions.stem: Fáwẹ̀lì iwájú ni
questions.explanation: Front vowels are [i], [e], [ẹ]; [u], [o], [ọ] are back vowels.

questions.stem: Sílébù mélòó ni ó wà nínú ọ̀rọ̀ "ìgbálẹ̀"?
questions.explanation: gb is a single consonant, so the word divides ì-gbá-lẹ̀: three syllables.

questions.stem: Ohùn mélòó ni ó wà nínú èdè Yorùbá?
questions.explanation: Yoruba has three tones: high (òkè), mid (àárín) and low (ìsàlẹ̀).

questions.stem: Ìlànà ohùn ọ̀rọ̀ "ọmọ" ni
questions.explanation: Both syllables of ọmọ carry mid tone, which is left unmarked in the orthography.

questions.stem: Nígbà tí "ní ilé" di "nílé", ìlànà ìró tí ó wáyé ni
questions.explanation: The vowel i of ilé is deleted: elision (ìpajẹ).

questions.stem: Ọ̀rọ̀ wo ni ó ní fáwẹ̀lì àránmúpè?
questions.explanation: The final "an" in ẹran is a nasal vowel; the others have only oral vowels.

questions.stem: Èwo ni ọ̀rọ̀-orúkọ?
questions.explanation: Ilé (house) is a noun; lọ is a verb, dáradára an adverb and àti a conjunction.

questions.stem: Nínú gbólóhùn "Adé ra ẹja ní ọjà", olùwà ni
questions.explanation: Adé performs the action, so it is the subject (olùwà).

questions.stem: Nínú gbólóhùn "Bọ́lá jẹ ìrẹsì", àbọ̀ ni
questions.explanation: Ìrẹsì receives the action of the verb: it is the object (àbọ̀).

questions.stem: Èwo ni ọ̀rọ̀-arọ́pò-orúkọ?
questions.explanation: Wọ́n (they) replaces a noun; kíákíá is an adverb, pupa describes, sí is a preposition.

questions.stem: "Mẹ́rìndínlógún" túmọ̀ sí
questions.explanation: Mẹ́rin dín ní ogún: four less than twenty = 16.

questions.stem: Ọ̀rọ̀-ìṣe tí a fi ṣẹ̀dá ọ̀rọ̀-orúkọ "olùkọ́" ni
questions.explanation: Olùkọ́ (teacher) is formed from the verb kọ́ (teach) with the prefix olù-.

questions.stem: Èwo nínú àwọn ọ̀rọ̀ wọ̀nyí ni a ṣẹ̀dá nípa fífi àfòmọ́ ìbẹ̀rẹ̀ kún ọ̀rọ̀-ìṣe?
questions.explanation: Ìrìn = ì- + rìn (walk); the others are basic, underived nouns.

questions.stem: Nínú gbólóhùn "Ọmọ náà ń kàwé", "ń" fi hàn pé iṣẹ́ náà
questions.explanation: The marker ń shows progressive aspect: the action is in progress.

questions.stem: Èwo ni ọ̀rọ̀-asopọ̀?
questions.explanation: Ṣùgbọ́n (but) joins clauses: a conjunction.

questions.stem: Ewì àwọn ọdẹ tí a fi ń júbà Ògún ni
questions.explanation: Ìjálá is the hunters' chant associated with Ògún.

questions.stem: Ẹ̀sà (ìwì) jẹ́ ewì àwọn
questions.explanation: Ẹ̀sà/ìwì is chanted by members of the egúngún (masquerade) cult.

questions.stem: Ewì tí ìyàwó máa ń sun nígbà tí ó bá ń lọ sí ilé ọkọ ni
questions.explanation: Ẹkún ìyàwó is the bride's chant on leaving her father's house.

questions.stem: Ìyàtọ̀ tí ó wà láàárín àlọ́ àpamọ̀ àti àlọ́ àpagbè ni pé àlọ́ àpamọ̀
options: jẹ́ ìbéèrè tí a ń retí ìdáhùn sí.
questions.explanation: Àlọ́ àpamọ̀ is a riddle that demands an answer; àlọ́ àpagbè is a folktale, often with songs.

questions.stem: Ẹni tí ó máa ń dá Ifá ni
questions.explanation: The babaláwo is the Ifá diviner; onílù is a drummer and alágbẹ̀dẹ a blacksmith.

questions.stem: Òrìṣà tí Ifá jẹ mọ́ ni
questions.explanation: Ifá divination is associated with Ọ̀rúnmìlà.

questions.stem: Ẹ̀wọ̀n tí wọ́n so èso mẹ́jọ mọ́, tí babaláwo fi ń dá Ifá ni
questions.explanation: The ọ̀pẹ̀lẹ̀ is the divining chain with eight half-seeds.

questions.stem: Òwe jẹ́
options: ọ̀rọ̀ ìjìnlẹ̀ tí ó kún fún ọgbọ́n àti ìrírí àwọn baba ńlá.
questions.explanation: Proverbs (òwe) are short, deep sayings carrying ancestral wisdom.

questions.stem: Ta ni ó kọ ìwé ìtàn àròsọ "Ògbójú Ọdẹ nínú Igbó Irúnmọlẹ̀"?
questions.explanation: D. O. Fágúnwà wrote this pioneering Yoruba novel (1938). Ṣóyínká translated it into English.

questions.stem: Ta ni ó kọ eré-onítàn "Efúnṣetán Aníwúrà"?
questions.explanation: Akínwùmí Ìṣọ̀lá wrote the play about the Ìyálóde of Ìbàdàn.

questions.stem: Àwọn tí ó kópa nínú ìtàn tàbí eré ni a ń pè ní
questions.explanation: Characters are ẹ̀dá-ìtàn; setting is ibùdó-ìtàn, theme kókó-ọ̀rọ̀, plot àhunpọ̀-ìtàn.

questions.stem: Ibi àti àkókò tí ìṣẹ̀lẹ̀ inú ìtàn ti wáyé ni
questions.explanation: The place and time of a story is its setting (ibùdó-ìtàn).

questions.stem: "Ọmọ náà ga bí igi ọ̀pẹ" jẹ́ àpẹẹrẹ
questions.explanation: A direct comparison using "bí" (like) is a simile (àfiwé tààrà).

questions.stem: Ọ̀nà-èdè tí a fi ń sọ ohun kan kọjá bí ó ṣe rí gan-an ni
questions.explanation: Exaggeration beyond reality is hyperbole (àsọdùn).

questions.stem: Orúkọ tí a máa ń sọ ọmọ tí ó fi ẹsẹ̀ wáyé nígbà ìbí ni
questions.explanation: Ìgè is the name for a child born feet first (breech).

questions.stem: Orúkọ tí a ń sọ ọmọ tí a bí tẹ̀lé ìbejì ni
questions.explanation: Ìdòwú is the child born after twins.

questions.stem: Bí ọmọkùnrin Yorùbá ṣe ń kí àgbàlagbà ni
questions.explanation: Boys prostrate (ìdọ̀bálẹ̀); girls kneel (ìkúnlẹ̀).

questions.stem: Oúnjẹ tí a fi èlùbọ́ ṣe ni
questions.explanation: Àmàlà is made from yam flour (èlùbọ́); ìyán is pounded yam.

questions.stem: Ọ̀nà tí àwọn ènìyàn fi ń dá owó jọ, tí ẹnì kọ̀ọ̀kan yóò sì gba gbogbo rẹ̀ ní àsìkò tirẹ̀ ni
questions.explanation: Èésú is a rotating savings scheme; ọ̀wẹ̀ is communal labour and ìdána a marriage payment.

questions.stem: Òrìṣà ààrá àti mànàmáná ni
questions.explanation: Ṣàngó is the deity of thunder and lightning.

questions.stem:
Kọ àròkọ tí kò dín ní ọ̀ọ́dúnrún ọ̀rọ̀ lórí ọ̀kan nínú àwọn orí-ọ̀rọ̀ wọ̀nyí:
(a) Ọjà ìlú mi.
(b) Ìdí tí ó fi yẹ kí gbogbo ọmọ lọ sí ilé-ìwé.
(c) Lẹ́tà sí ọ̀rẹ́ rẹ tí ó ń gbé ní ìlú mìíràn nípa ìsinmi rẹ. [25 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
10 marks: Content (Àkóónú): relevant, well-developed ideas appropriate to the essay type chosen
5 marks: Organisation (Ìhun): introduction, logical paragraphs, conclusion; correct letter format (address, date, salutation, closing) for (c)
7 marks: Expression (Ìlò èdè): idiomatic Yoruba, proverbs and varied sentences used appropriately
3 marks: Mechanical accuracy: correct official orthography, tone marks and punctuation
questions.explanation: A strong answer chooses one topic, plans an introduction, three or four focused paragraphs and a conclusion, uses rich idiomatic Yoruba with apt proverbs, and writes in the official orthography with correct tone marks.

questions.stem:
(a) Ṣàlàyé ohun tí sílébù jẹ́. [3 marks]
(b) Kọ ìhun sílébù mẹ́ta tí ó wà nínú èdè Yorùbá, kí o sì fún ọ̀kọ̀ọ̀kan ní àpẹẹrẹ méjì. [9 marks]
(c) Pín àwọn ọ̀rọ̀ wọ̀nyí sí sílébù: ìgbálẹ̀, àǹfààní, ọmọ. [3 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: Syllable: a unit of pronunciation uttered with one tone, consisting of a vowel, consonant + vowel, or a syllabic nasal
3 marks: V (fáwẹ̀lì nìkan): e.g. the first syllables of ọmọ, ìyá
3 marks: KF (kọ́ńsónáǹtì + fáwẹ̀lì): e.g. bá, lọ, gbá
3 marks: N (kọ́ńsónáǹtì àránmúpè aṣesílébù): e.g. the ǹ in àǹfààní, ń in "ó ń lọ"
1 mark: ì-gbá-lẹ̀
1 mark: à-ǹ-fà-à-ní
1 mark: ọ-mọ
questions.explanation: Yoruba syllables are V, CV or syllabic N, each bearing a tone; there are no closed syllables or clusters. ìgbálẹ̀ = ì-gbá-lẹ̀; àǹfààní = à-ǹ-fà-à-ní; ọmọ = ọ-mọ.

questions.stem: Ṣàlàyé márùn-ún nínú ìsọ̀rí ọ̀rọ̀ Yorùbá, kí o sì fún ọ̀kọ̀ọ̀kan ní àpẹẹrẹ méjì. [15 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: Ọ̀rọ̀-orúkọ (noun): names person, place, thing; e.g. ilé, Adé, ajá
3 marks: Ọ̀rọ̀-ìṣe (verb): shows action or state; e.g. lọ, jẹ, sùn
3 marks: Ọ̀rọ̀-arọ́pò-orúkọ (pronoun): replaces a noun; e.g. mo, wọ́n, òun
3 marks: Ọ̀rọ̀-àpèjúwe (qualifier/adjective): describes a noun; e.g. pupa, dúdú, ńlá
3 marks: Any other class explained with examples, e.g. ọ̀rọ̀-àpọ́nlé (adverb: kíákíá, dáadáa), ọ̀rọ̀-asopọ̀ (conjunction: àti, ṣùgbọ́n, tàbí), ọ̀rọ̀-atọ́kùn (preposition: ní, sí)
questions.explanation: Five classes, each defined with two examples: noun (ilé, ajá), verb (lọ, jẹ), pronoun (mo, wọ́n), qualifier (pupa, ńlá), adverb (kíákíá) or conjunction (àti, ṣùgbọ́n).

questions.stem:
(a) Àwọn wo ni ó máa ń sun ìjálá? [2 marks]
(b) Ìgbà wo ni a máa ń sun ìjálá? Kọ àsìkò méjì. [4 marks]
(c) Ṣàlàyé àbùdá ìjálá mẹ́ta. [9 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: Hunters (ọdẹ) and devotees of Ògún
4 marks: Any two (2 each): Ògún festival; gatherings of hunters; funeral rites of a hunter; social occasions/entertainment of hunters
9 marks: Any three explained (3 each): praise of Ògún (oríkì Ògún); praise/description of animals and their habits; oríkì of lineages and persons; chanted in a distinctive high-pitched voice; long lines with repetition and parallelism; use of proverbs, imagery and wordplay
questions.explanation: Ìjálá is chanted by hunters and Ògún devotees at Ògún festivals, hunters' gatherings and funerals. It praises Ògún, animals and lineages, uses a distinctive chanting voice, repetition, imagery and proverbs.

questions.stem:
(a) Kí ni ìtàn àròsọ? [3 marks]
(b) Ṣàlàyé àwọn èròjà ìtàn àròsọ wọ̀nyí: ẹ̀dá-ìtàn, ibùdó-ìtàn, àhunpọ̀-ìtàn àti kókó-ọ̀rọ̀. [12 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: Ìtàn àròsọ: written prose fiction (novel/story) created from the author's imagination
3 marks: Ẹ̀dá-ìtàn: the characters who act in the story (main and minor characters)
3 marks: Ibùdó-ìtàn: the setting, place and time in which the events occur
3 marks: Àhunpọ̀-ìtàn: the plot, the arrangement of events from beginning to end
3 marks: Kókó-ọ̀rọ̀: the theme, the main message or idea of the work
questions.explanation: Ìtàn àròsọ is imaginative prose fiction. Its elements: characters (ẹ̀dá-ìtàn), setting (ibùdó-ìtàn), plot (àhunpọ̀-ìtàn) and theme (kókó-ọ̀rọ̀).

questions.stem:
(a) Ṣàlàyé bí àwọn Yorùbá ṣe ń ṣe ìsọmọlórúkọ. [7 marks]
(b) Dárúkọ ohun èlò mẹ́rin tí a ń lò níbi ìsọmọlórúkọ, kí o sì sọ ìtumọ̀ ọ̀kọ̀ọ̀kan. [8 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
7 marks: Description (award up to 7): held some days after birth (traditionally the 7th, 8th or 9th day depending on sex/locality); family and friends gather early; an elder prays and introduces items; child named (orúkọ àmútọ̀runwá, àbísọ, oríkì); child's feet touched to ground/water; prayers, feasting and gifts
8 marks: Any four items with meaning (2 each): oyin (honey) - sweet life; iyọ̀ (salt) - life full of flavour; omi (water) - no enemy can stop water; orógbó (bitter kola) - long life; obì (kola) - to ward off evil/death; epo (palm oil) - smooth life; ataare (alligator pepper) - many children; ẹja - free movement/success
questions.explanation: Relatives gather some days after birth; an elder offers prayers with symbolic items and pronounces the names. Honey for sweetness, salt for flavour, water for unstoppable progress, bitter kola for long life, kola to ward off evil, alligator pepper for many children.
